svg.title: Timeline of Pakistan's constitutional development and citizen rights
svg.desc: Timeline of Pakistan's constitutional development showing the 1956, 1962, and 1973 constitutions, followed by the 2010 Eighteenth Amendment which introduced Article 25A and Article 19A for citizens.
svg.text: Milestones in Pakistan's constitutional rights
1956: First Constitution of Pakistan
Declared Pakistan an Islamic Republic. Included a formal chapter of
fundamental rights enforceable by courts. Abrogated in October 1958.
1962: Second Constitution
Introduced a presidential system with indirect elections. Fundamental rights
were initially omitted, then restored by the First Amendment in 1963.
1973: Third Constitution (Consensus Framework)
Enacted on 14 August 1973 by unanimous parliamentary consensus. Created a
federal parliamentary democracy and placed comprehensive Fundamental Rights
in Articles 8 to 28, enforceable through High Courts (Article 199).
2010: Eighteenth Amendment (Expanding Rights)
Major cross-party reform adding Article 25A (right to free and compulsory
education, ages 5 to 16), Article 19A (right to information), and Article 10A
(right to fair trial). Strengthened provincial autonomy.
Today: Supreme Law and Enforceable Protections
The Constitution remains the supreme legal authority. Superior courts protect
fundamental rights while Article 5 binds every citizen to state loyalty and law.
The 1973 Constitution forms the living legal foundation of citizen rights in Pakistan.
